content:
incident-bot: Pager: redis-cache-auth-errors > 10% for rate-limiter-prefix in us-east-1. Severity: P1. Escalation: eng-oncall -> eng-sre. (auto: 1740001234)

sachin: I'm on it. seeing spikes in 401s from redis provider (auth failed). rate limiter shards throwing errors and falling back to 503s.

emily: +1, I'm switching user-facing routes to degraded mode (less strict throttling) to avoid cascading 5xxs. will toggle feature flag now.

ivan: Can you paste the exact redis error? I want to check client retry behavior.

sachin: logs: ```
ERR Client sent AUTH, but no password is set
connection_id=237829 host=10.8.1.47:6379
```
This matches a provider-side auth rotation / token expiry pattern. happening across 3 clusters in us-east-1.

emily: Toggling flag 'rl:fallback-local' -> true (now). Local in-memory token-buckets will be used for ~5m for the most affected routes.

ops-bot: deploy started: roll /feature/rl-fallback-local -> prod (id: deploy-789).

molly: Heads-up to CS: some customers might see rate-limiter failures resulting in longer timeouts for embed/ingest endpoints. I'm drafting a short message for affected accounts.

ivan: Good call. Also, let's cut writes to cache for non-critical keys. Switch caching writes to best-effort mode. Command: ```curl -X POST https://internal-config/feature -d '{"key":"cache:writes","mode":"best-effort"}'```

sachin: Done. cache writes = best-effort. Verified no new write errors. Read errors still 401-ish.

derek: Any impact on latency dashboards? Observability vendor is showing a bunch of `cache_miss` alerts too. Could be due to cold fallback.

ivan: Tracing shows increased latency at our rate-limiter service where it waits on cache RPCs -> times out -> 503. With local fallback enabled, tail latencies dropped 60ms so far.

incident-bot: Note: opened incident record INC-2026-0456. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-0456

sachin: Contacting third-party support (RedisCloud): support ticket #RC-91342. Sent logs and auth failure samples. ETA unknown.

molly: I've queued proactive emails for accounts with high QPS. Draft pinned in #customer-updates.

emily: On-call handoff in 40m. I'll summarize current mitigations in the handoff message: local RB fallback, cache writes best-effort, feature flag active, monitoring adjusted.

ivan: Quick mitigation checklist for handoff:
- keep 'rl:fallback-local' = true
- set cache TTLs to low for writes that succeeded to avoid stale data
- reduce rate-limiter strictness for non-critical endpoints
- escalate to vendor support with auth-token logs and region-specific timestamps

sachin: Adding an emergency circuit-breaker for rate-limiter -> if >20% RPC failures in 1m then serve soft-allow (increment local counters) and emit a metric `rl.soft_allow`. Implemented.

ops-bot: alerting rule updated: suspend automated remediations for cache-write anomalies while incident active.

molly: CS note: "We are seeing transient cache auth failures in us-east-1 affecting rate limiting. We've applied a local fallback and mitigations to maintain service. We'll update as we hear back from the cache provider." Will send in 5.

derek: Any customer-visible 5xx counts? We need to quantify impact for the incident severity.

ivan: temporary numbers: ~1200 requests/min with short 503 spike window; estimated affected requests ~0.6% of peak traffic in last 10m. Most requests now served via local fallback.

sachin: Provider reply: "We've identified a token rotation issue in our auth proxy affecting a subset of clients in us-east-1. Rollback in progress." (from RC support, ticket RC-91342).

emily: Good. Keep fallback up for 15 more mins after provider confirms stable. I'll prepare rollback steps for our fallback (so we don't flip-flop).

molly: Sent CS note and opened a customer-impact row in the incident doc: affected customers (high-QPS) listed, estimated window 1740001000 -> TBD.

ivan: Small postmortem bullet: add monitoring that correlates provider auth error counts with our cache RPC latency and rate-limiter failures so future detection is clearer.

sachin: Handoff: I'm handing oncall to emily at 1740005000. Current state: provider rolling back rotation, fallback active, cache writes best-effort, `rl.soft_allow` metric enabled. No active customer tickets requiring immediate mitigation.

emily: Taking over. I'll keep monitoring for 30m then start safe rollback sequence if provider confirms.

incident-bot: Handoff recorded: oncall_from=sachin oncall_to=emily at 1740005000.

ops-bot: scheduled postmortem meeting created: 1740080000 (roughly 22h), invite sent to eng-sre, eng-runtime, customer-success.

molly: I'll follow up with affected customers after final window closed.

derek: Action items captured in incident doc: 1) Add auth-rotation correlation alert 2) Make local fallback an automated mitigation (safe by default) 3) Review provider client config (use long-lived certs/refresh flows)

sachin: Closing note before handoff: If provider goes into a prolonged outage, plan B is routing rate-limiter reads to a read-replica cluster in a different region plus long-term local counters synced to DB. Not ideal but buys time.

emily: Acknowledged. I'll keep this thread updated with provider final confirmation + rollback time.

ops-bot: incident status -> mitigated (partial)."
